purpose: Portable semantic boundary between event-specific source normalization and reusable race analysis UI/engines.
principles: Source observations are never fabricated to satisfy a feature.
Race family does not imply identical course geometry.
Feature availability is capability-driven per race edition.
Missing demographic, identity, checkpoint or route evidence remains missing.
Replay interpolation is presentation-only and never becomes a source split.
Cross-year identity requires explicit confidence-bearing evidence.
Event-specific source acquisition remains outside the engine contract.

capabilities.runner_profile: Requires a person or team result record.
capabilities.sex_filter: Requires source-backed sex coverage sufficient for the view.
capabilities.age_analysis: Requires source-backed age or age-category data appropriate to the view.
capabilities.club_analysis: Requires source-backed club/location values appropriate to the view.
capabilities.segment_analysis: Requires at least two observed analysis boundaries for relevant records.
capabilities.replay: Requires observed timing anchors plus a locally usable route asset.
capabilities.head_to_head: Requires compatible observed timing data for compared entries.
capabilities.person_history: Requires a separate verified/confidence-bearing cross-edition identity layer.
capabilities.goal_pace: Requires a race for which a finish-time target is semantically meaningful.
capabilities.team_members: Requires source-backed team/member rows; does not imply leg assignment.

rules: A race family is not a course version.
Whole-course performance comparison requires identical course_version or an explicit comparison group/method.
Geometry evidence and redistributable local route assets are separate concepts.
No route-dependent feature may be enabled solely because another edition in the family has geometry.
Retain source labels alongside normalized semantics.
Only observed/published timing passages are source splits.
Auxiliary or display-only points must not silently become analysis boundaries.
Source-local result identity never implies cross-year person identity.
Name equality alone is insufficient for cross-year linkage.
Cross-year person keys must preserve evidence/confidence and ambiguity handling.
Team names never become person identities.

loading.minimum: An implementation may load one complete payload.
loading.rule: Progressive loading is an optimization; all hydration phases must preserve semantic parity with the complete payload.
